summary: Prioritize the Field Guide review client as the top architecture-deepening candidate.
context: Recent commits repeatedly changed Field Guide browser behavior. Its implementation is embedded as a large inline string and most UI tests assert source substrings, producing weak locality and low test leverage.

options.label: Deepen the Field Guide review client first
Deepen Markdown Share Editor Workspace first
options.rejectedBecause: It has strong leverage, but the Field Guide browser has newer churn and weaker behavioral test coverage.

options.label: Consolidate cross-backend decision-record invariants first
options.rejectedBecause: It requires more care around documented backend responsibilities and has a wider persistence blast radius.

choice: Deepen the Field Guide review client first.
rationale: Deleting the inline-string boundary concentrates state, rendering, commands, and DOM behavior in an executable browser module. It directly improves the newest hot spot and replaces source-text assertions with behavioral tests.
consequences: The server retains a small page and CSP shell.
Review behavior becomes directly executable in tests.
The CSS asset becomes the single styling source for the review browser.

evidence.excerpt: apps/field-guide-console/src/ui.ts embeds the browser application and styling in one template-string boundary.
Recent Field Guide changes and substring-oriented UI tests make this the highest-leverage hot spot.
